draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Poovar! The Neyyar River, a freshwater lake, the backwater canals and the Arabian Sea all meet here within a few hundred metres of each other.
draft.hungryLine: Seafood rules in Poovar. Order karimeen pollichathu, pearl spot fish baked in banana leaf with spiced coconut paste.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Take a boat to the Poovar Estuary and Golden Sand Beach, gliding through the mangrove canals on the way.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Golden Sand Beach can only be reached by boat, so it's one of the least crowded beaches in Kerala.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Poovar's central mosque was built by Malik Deenar, an eighth-century Muslim preacher.

legends.title: River of Flowers
legends.body: Marthanda Varma, the 18th-century king of Travancore, named Poovar for the fragrant flowers that once floated down the Neyyar to the sea. Poo means flower and ar means river.

legends.title: King Solomon's ships
legends.body: It's believed that ships owned by King Solomon of Israel landed at Ophir. Some sources identify Ophir as Poovar.

tips.title: Go out at dawn.
tips.body: Early boat trips give the best bird sightings, and the estuary looks its best at dawn and dusk.

tips.title: Drink bottled water.
tips.body: Tap water here isn't potable, so stick to bottled or filtered water.

story.title: A port of spices
story.body: Poovar traded timber, sandalwood, ivory and spices. Megasthenes, Pliny the Elder and Marco Polo mention its links with Greece and Rome.

story.title: Malik Deenar's mosque
story.body: Poovar was one of the ancient Muslim settlements on India's west coast. Its central mosque was built by Malik Deenar, an eighth-century preacher.

story.title: A major port
story.body: During the reign of the Chola dynasty, Poovar was a major port.

story.title: A new name
story.body: The place was called Pokkumoosapuram until Marthanda Varma renamed it Poovar, the River of Flowers.

story.title: Quiet backwaters
story.body: Poovar draws travellers who want backwaters without the bustle of Alleppey or Kumarakom. Up the coast, a deep-water container terminal is changing Vizhinjam harbour.
